### Wintrust Financial Corporation Reports Record Net Income


October 19, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s205.q4cdn.com/387403231/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/Wintrust-Financial-Corporation-Q3-2026-Earnings-Release.pdf)


ROSEMONT, Ill., Oct. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Wintrust Financial Corporation (“Wintrust”, “the Company”, “we” or “our”) (Nasdaq: WTFC) announced record net income of $700.1 million, or $9.89 per diluted common share, for the first nine months of 2026 compared to net income of $600.8 million, or $8.25 per diluted common share, for the same period of 2025. This represents a year-to-date net income increase of 17% compared to the same period of 2025. Pre-tax, pre-provision income (non-GAAP) for the first nine months of the year totaled a record $1.0 billion, compared to $884.1 million for the first nine months of 2025.


The Company reported record quarterly net income of $239.1 million, or $3.37 per diluted common share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to net income of $233.7 million, or $3.30 per diluted common share, for the second quarter of 2026. Pre-tax, pre-provision income (non-GAAP) for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $352.2 million, as compared to $341.1 million for the second quarter of 2026.


Timothy S. Crane, President and Chief Executive Officer, commented, “Our strong momentum in the first half of the year continued into the third quarter leading to consistent and record results for the first nine months of 2026. The third quarter of 2026 produced the seventh consecutive quarter of record net income for the Company.”


Additionally, Mr. Crane noted, “Net interest income came in at $621.6 million for the quarter, an increase of $24.2 million, or 16% annualized, from the second quarter of 2026. Net interest margin of 3.51% in the third quarter remained in line with our expectations, and we believe our balance sheet is well positioned to support stable performance through changing interest rate environments.”


**Highlights of the third quarter of 2026:**
*Comparative information to the* *second quarter of 2026* *, unless otherwise noted*


- Total loans increased by $1.1 billion, or 8% annualized.
- Total deposits increased by $1.3 billion, or 8% annualized.
- Total assets increased by $1.3 billion, or 7% annualized.
- Net interest income increased to $621.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $597.4 million in the second quarter of 2026, driven by strong average earning asset growth.


- Net interest margin was 3.49% (3.51% on a fully taxable-equivalent basis, non-GAAP) during the third quarter of 2026 which was in line with our prior guidance.


- Provision for credit losses totaled $25.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $23.1 million in the second quarter of 2026.
- Net charge-offs totaled $21.0 million, or 15 basis points of average total loans on an annualized basis, in the third quarter of 2026 up from $13.4 million, or 10 basis points of average total loans on an annualized basis, in the second quarter of 2026.
- Non-performing loans totaled $176.9 million and comprised 0.31% of total loans at September 30, 2026, as compared to $179.3 million and 0.32% of total loans at June 30, 2026.


“We are encouraged by our strong third quarter performance and record results year-to-date. We believe we are well-positioned to build on our strong momentum and deliver further revenue growth as we close out the year. Our unique market position and strong customer relationships continue to create long-term franchise value in the markets we serve. We are proud of our latest deposit market share gains in Illinois and remain committed to expanding our market presence in Wisconsin and west Michigan. Our focus remains on delivering consistent balance sheet growth, expanding net interest income while maintaining a disciplined approach to expense management, which should generate positive operating leverage for the year”, Mr. Crane concluded.

**SUMMARY OF RESULTS:**


**BALANCE SHEET**


Total assets increased $1.3 billion in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2026, driven by a $1.1 billion increase in total loans. The robust loan growth was diversified across all major loan portfolios.


Total liabilities increased by $1.5 billion in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2026, driven by a $1.3 billion increase in total deposits. Strong organic deposit growth in the third quarter of 2026 was driven by our diverse customer base and product offerings. Non-interest bearing deposit balances represented 19% of total deposits and average non-interest bearing deposit balances have remained stable in recent quarters. The Company's loans-to-deposits ratio ended the quarter at 91.0%.


For more information regarding changes in the Company’s balance sheet, see Consolidated Statements of Condition and Table 1 through Table 3 in this report.


**NET INTEREST INCOME**


For the third quarter of 2026, net interest income totaled $621.6 million, compared to $597.4 million in the second quarter of 2026. The increase in net interest income in the third quarter of 2026 was driven by strong average earning asset growth of $2.1 billion.


Net interest margin was 3.49% (3.51% on a fully taxable-equivalent basis, non-GAAP) during the third quarter of 2026, down one basis point compared to the second quarter of 2026. The yield on earning assets remained flat during the third quarter of 2026 while loan yields decreased by one basis point. Funding cost on interest-bearing deposits decreased one basis point compared to the second quarter of 2026. The net free funds contribution in the third quarter of 2026 decreased two basis points compared to the second quarter of 2026.


For more information regarding net interest income, see Table 4 through Table 8 in this report.


**ASSET QUALITY**


The allowance for credit losses totaled $486.1 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase from $481.2 million as of June 30, 2026. A provision for credit losses totaling $25.9 million was recorded for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $23.1 million recorded in the second quarter of 2026. The provision for credit losses recognized in the third quarter of 2026 reflects growth in the portfolio, stable credit quality and a mostly stable macroeconomic forecast. However, given future economic performance remains uncertain, allowance results capture uncertainty related to credit spreads, equity market valuations, consumer & business sentiment, and the job market. For more information regarding the allowance for credit losses and provision for credit losses, see Table 11 in this report.


Management believes the allowance for credit losses is appropriate to account for expected credit losses. The Company is required to estimate expected credit losses over the life of the Company’s financial assets as of the reporting date. There can be no assurances, however, that future losses will not significantly exceed the amounts provided for, thereby affecting future results of operations. A summary of the allowance for credit losses calculated for the loan components in each portfolio as of September 30, 2026, June 30, 2026, and March 31, 2026 is shown on Table 12 of this report.


Net charge-offs totaled $21.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $7.6 million compared to $13.4 million of net charge-offs in the second quarter of 2026. Net charge-offs as a percentage of average total loans were 15 basis points in the third quarter of 2026 on an annualized basis compared to 10 basis points on an annualized basis in the second quarter of 2026. For more information regarding net charge-offs, see Table 10 in this report.


The Company’s loan portfolio delinquency rates remain low. For more information regarding past due loans, see Table 13 in this report.


Non-performing assets and non-performing loans were stable compared to prior quarter. Non-performing assets totaled $193.3 million and comprised 0.25% of total assets as of September 30, 2026, as compared to $195.2 million, or 0.26% of total assets, as of June 30, 2026. Non-performing loans totaled $176.9 million and comprised 0.31% of total loans at September 30, 2026, as compared to $179.3 million and 0.32% of total loans at June 30, 2026. For more information regarding non-performing assets, see Table 14 in this report.


**NON-INTEREST INCOME**


Non-interest income totaled $136.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $141.3 million in the second quarter of 2026.


Wealth management revenue increased by approximately $1.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to the second quarter of 2026. The increase in the third quarter of 2026 was primarily driven by increased trust and asset management fees from higher assets under management during the period. Wealth management revenue is comprised of the trust and asset management revenue of Wintrust Private Trust Company and Great Lakes Advisors, the brokerage commissions, managed money fees and insurance product commissions at Wintrust Investments and fees from tax-deferred like-kind exchange services provided by the Chicago Deferred Exchange Company.


Mortgage banking revenue totaled $25.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $27.4 million in the second quarter of 2026. The decrease in the third quarter of 2026 was primarily attributed to lower mortgage loan originations and related operational revenue. For more information regarding mortgage banking revenue, see Table 16 in this report.


The Company recognized approximately $1.6 million in net losses on investment securities in the third quarter of 2026 compared to approximately $1.8 million in net gains in the second quarter of 2026. The net losses in the third quarter of 2026 were primarily the result of fair value adjustments on the Company’s equity investment securities with a readily determinable fair value.


For more information regarding non-interest income, see Table 15 in this report.


**NON-INTEREST EXPENSE**


Non-interest expense totaled $405.7 million in the third quarter of 2026, increasing $8.1 million, compared to $397.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. Non-interest expense, as a percent of average assets, decreased to 2.16% in the third quarter of 2026 from 2.21% in the second quarter of 2026.


Salaries and employee benefits expense decreased by approximately $3.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to the second quarter of 2026. This was primarily driven by lower payroll taxes and deferred compensation expense during the third quarter of 2026.


Advertising and marketing expense in the third quarter of 2026 totaled $21.8 million, which was a $1.4 million increase as compared to the second quarter of 2026. The increase in the third quarter was primarily driven by community sponsorship events and media commitments which are historically higher in the second and third quarter of the year. Marketing costs are incurred to promote the Company’s brand, commercial banking capabilities and the Company’s various products, to attract loans and deposits and to announce new branch openings as well as the expansion of the Company’s non-bank businesses. The level of marketing expenditures depends on the timing of sponsorship programs utilized which are determined based on the market area, targeted audience, competition and various other factors. Generally, these expenses are elevated in the second and third quarters of each year.


FDIC insurance totaled $12.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, a $5.5 million increase from the second quarter of 2026. This was primarily the result of the $5.2 million FDIC special assessment reversal recorded in the second quarter of 2026. The special assessments were in response to certain bank failures in 2023 and the reversal was based on the FDIC's final determination of losses to its Deposit Insurance Fund.


For more information regarding non-interest expense, see Table 17 in this report.


**INCOME TAXES**


The Company recorded income tax expense of $87.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $84.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. The effective tax rates were 26.7% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 26.5% in the second quarter of 2026.


**BUSINESS SUMMARY**


*Community Banking*


Through community banking, the Company provides banking and financial services primarily to individuals, small to mid-sized businesses, local governmental units and institutional clients residing primarily in the local areas the Company services. In the third quarter of 2026, community banking increased its commercial, commercial real estate and residential real estate loan portfolios.


Mortgage banking revenue was $25.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $1.9 million compared to the second quarter of 2026. See Table 16 for more detail. Service charges on deposit accounts totaled $22.2 million in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to $21.2 million in the second quarter of 2026. The Company’s gross commercial and commercial real estate loan pipelines remained solid as of September 30, 2026 indicating momentum for expected continued loan growth in the fourth quarter of 2026.


*Specialty Finance*


Through specialty finance, the Company offers financing of insurance premiums for businesses and individuals, equipment financing through structured loans and lease products to customers in a variety of industries, accounts receivable financing and value-added, out-sourced administrative services and other services. Originations within the insurance premium financing receivables portfolios were approximately $5.4 billion during the third quarter of 2026. Average balances increased by $781.7 million, as compared to the second quarter of 2026. The Company’s leasing divisions’ portfolio balances increased in the third quarter of 2026, with capital leases, loans, and equipment on operating leases of $3.1 billion, $1.3 billion, and $363.2 million as of September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $3.1 billion, $1.2 billion, and $363.7 million as of June 30, 2026, respectively. Revenues from the Company’s out-sourced administrative services business were $1.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, which was relatively stable compared to the second quarter of 2026.


*Wealth Management*


Through wealth management, the Company offers a full range of wealth management services, including trust and investment services, tax-deferred like-kind exchange services, asset management, and securities brokerage services. Wealth management revenue totaled $41.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, an increase as compared to the second quarter of 2026. At September 30, 2026, the Company’s wealth management subsidiaries had approximately $51.5 billion of assets under administration, which excludes assets owned by the Company and its subsidiary banks.


**ITEMS IMPACTING COMPARATIVE FINANCIAL RESULTS**


*Business Acquisition*


On September 1, 2026, the Company completed its purchase of the guardianship services business that was previously announced (the “business”). The business has approximately $1.2 billion in assets under management. As of September 30, 2026, the Company preliminarily recorded goodwill of approximately $7.5 million. In accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), the initial purchase accounting for this business acquisition is not finalized and is therefore subject to change.

**TABLE 8: INTEREST RATE SENSITIVITY**


As an ongoing part of its financial strategy, the Company attempts to manage the impact of fluctuations in market interest rates on net interest income. Management measures its exposure to changes in interest rates by modeling many different interest rate scenarios.

**TABLE 18:** **SUPPLEMENTAL NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES/RATIOS**


The accounting and reporting policies of Wintrust conform to generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) in the United States and prevailing practices in the banking industry. However, certain non-GAAP performance measures and ratios are used by management to evaluate and measure the Company’s performance. These include taxable-equivalent net interest income (including its individual components), taxable-equivalent net interest margin (including its individual components), the taxable-equivalent efficiency ratio, tangible common equity ratio, tangible book value per common share, return on average tangible common equity, and pre-tax income, excluding provision for credit losses. Management believes that these measures and ratios provide users of the Company’s financial information a more meaningful view of the performance of the Company’s interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities and of the Company’s operating efficiency. Other financial holding companies may define or calculate these measures and ratios differently.


Management reviews yields on certain asset categories and the net interest margin of the Company and its banking subsidiaries on a fully taxable-equivalent basis (“FTE”). In this non-GAAP presentation, net interest income is adjusted to reflect tax-exempt interest income on an equivalent before-tax basis using tax rates effective as of the end of the period. This measure ensures comparability of net interest income arising from both taxable and tax-exempt sources. Net interest income on a FTE basis is also used in the calculation of the Company’s efficiency ratio. The efficiency ratio, which is calculated by dividing non-interest expense by total taxable-equivalent net revenue (less securities gains or losses), measures how much it costs to produce one dollar of revenue. Securities gains or losses are excluded from this calculation to better match revenue from daily operations to operational expenses. Management considers the tangible common equity ratio and tangible book value per common share as useful measurements of the Company’s equity. The Company references the return on average tangible common equity as a measurement of profitability. Management considers pre-tax income, excluding provision for credit losses, as a useful measurement of the Company’s core net income.
